title: Where religions began
examples: Why did so many religions start in Asia?

figure.label: Birthplaces of the world's major religions

explain.say: Almost all of the world's biggest religions began in one part of the world, Asia. Look at the map: the pins cluster in three regions, the Middle East, India and East Asia.

draw.label: Three cradles: the Middle East, India and East Asia

explain.say: In the Middle East began the Abrahamic religions. Judaism grew in the land of Israel more than 3,000 years ago, Christianity began around Jerusalem in the first century, and Islam began in Mecca and Medina in the 600s.

draw.label: The Abrahamic faiths: Judaism, Christianity, Islam

draw.text: All three honour Abraham, and Jerusalem is holy to all three.

explain.say: In India began Hinduism, with roots over 3,000 years old, then Buddhism and Jainism around 2,500 years ago, and Sikhism in the Punjab in the 1400s. The Buddha was born at Lumbini, in today's Nepal.

draw.text: Guru Nanak, the first Sikh Guru, was born in 1469 at Nankana Sahib.

explain.say: In East Asia, the teachings of Confucius began at Qufu in China around 2,500 years ago, Daoism grew in China too, and Shinto grew from the ancient traditions of Japan.

draw.text: Shinto has no single founder; Ise is its most sacred shrine.

explain.say: Persia, today's Iran, gave the world Zoroastrianism, one of the oldest faiths still followed, and much later, in the 1800s, the Bahá'í faith, whose world centre is now in Haifa.
Put in time order, the story stretches across more than three thousand years, and every one of these faiths is still alive today, carried far beyond the place where it began.

items: over 3,000 years ago: Hindu roots and early Judaism
about 500 BCE: the Buddha, Mahavira, Confucius

faq.a: Buddhism began in northern India about 2,500 years ago. Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, was born at Lumbini in today's Nepal, became enlightened at Bodh Gaya, and gave his first teaching at Sarnath, near Varanasi.
asks: which country did Buddhism come from

faq.a: Christianity began in the first century in the land of Judea and Galilee, today Israel and the Palestinian territories. Christians believe Jesus was born in Bethlehem; he taught in Galilee and was crucified in Jerusalem around the year 30. His followers then carried the faith across the Roman Empire.
asks: which country did Christianity begin in

faq.a: Islam began in Arabia in the 600s. Muslims believe the Prophet Muhammad received the first revelation of the Qur'an near Mecca in 610. In 622 he moved to Medina, and that journey, the Hijra, marks year one of the Islamic calendar.
asks: where was the Prophet Muhammad from
which country did Islam come from

faq.a: Hinduism grew up in the Indian subcontinent over thousands of years. It has no single founder or starting date; its oldest scriptures, the Vedas, were composed more than 3,000 years ago, and many traditions flowed together to form it.

Judaism began among the ancient Israelites in the land of Israel, more than 3,000 years ago. Jewish tradition traces the people back to Abraham and to the covenant at Mount Sinai given through Moses, and Jerusalem became its holy city.
asks: where did the Jewish religion start

faq.a: Sikhism began in the Punjab region of South Asia, which today crosses India and Pakistan. Its first Guru, Guru Nanak, was born in 1469 at Nankana Sahib, and nine more Gurus followed him.

Jainism comes from India. Its best-known teacher, Mahavira, lived around the same time as the Buddha, about 2,500 years ago. Jains see him as the last of twenty-four great teachers called Tirthankaras, so they regard the faith as even older.

faq.q: Where did Confucianism and Daoism begin?
faq.a: Both began in ancient China. Confucius lived from about 551 to 479 BCE and came from Qufu in today's Shandong province. Daoism is linked to the sage Laozi and the book called the Daodejing.

Shinto is the ancient native tradition of Japan. It has no founder; it grew from the honouring of kami, the sacred spirits of nature, places and ancestors. The Grand Shrine at Ise is its most sacred site.

faq.q: Why did so many religions start in Asia?
faq.a: Asia was home to some of the first big cities, kingdoms, writing systems and trade routes, so ideas could be written down and carried far. Historians also notice that many great teachers lived in the same era, around 800 to 200 BCE, which the philosopher Karl Jaspers called the Axial Age.
asks: why are most religions from the Middle East and India
why did religions start in the same place

faq.a: It is hard to say, because religions grow slowly. Hinduism is often called the oldest major religion still practised, with roots more than 3,000 years old, and Judaism and Zoroastrianism are also very old. Many local and Indigenous traditions may be older still.
asks: what is the oldest religion in the world

faq.q: Which is the newest world religion?
faq.a: Of the large world religions, Sikhism is the youngest, begun by Guru Nanak in the 1400s. The Bahá'í faith is younger still: it began in Iran in the 1800s.

Zoroastrianism began in ancient Iran, then called Persia, with the prophet Zarathustra, also called Zoroaster. Scholars debate when he lived. Today Zoroastrians live in Iran, around cities like Yazd, and in India, where they are known as Parsis.

faq.q: Why do Judaism, Christianity and Islam begin in the same region?
faq.a: They are related: all three trace their story back to Abraham and worship one God, so they are called the Abrahamic religions. Christianity grew from within Judaism, and Islam recognises earlier prophets such as Abraham, Moses and Jesus. That is why Jerusalem is holy to all three.
asks: why are the Abrahamic religions from the Middle East
are Judaism Christianity and Islam related
why is Jerusalem holy to three religions

facts: The Buddha was born at Lumbini, in today's Nepal, and became enlightened at Bodh Gaya in India.
Guru Nanak, the first Sikh Guru, was born in 1469 at Nankana Sahib, in today's Pakistan.
Muslims date the first revelation of the Qur'an to 610 CE, near Mecca; the Hijra to Medina in 622 begins the Islamic calendar.
Confucius lived from about 551 to 479 BCE and came from Qufu in China.
The Bahá'í faith began in Iran in the 1800s; its world centre is in Haifa.

quiz.show: Why has Hinduism no single starting date?

options.show: It grew slowly from many traditions, with no single founder
options.say: It grew slowly from many traditions, with no single founder
